newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rise 3.84 pct by lunch on IMF talks.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rise 3.84 pct by lunch on IMF talks.

text.p: Thai stocks soared in a lively Monday morning session as investors bought on growing hopes the IMF was about to help manage the ailing economy, brokers said.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya will meet IMF officials for talks this week and has promised to put a economic rescue package before cabinet within a week.
The SET Index rose 24.80 points or 3.84 percent to 671.38 by the lunch break. The SET 50 added 2.42 points or 4.96 percent in trade worth 4.95 billion baht.

Though an IMF-sponsored rescue plan was likely to include harsh medicine for the ailing Thai economy, the news was greeted by investors who fear a domestically engineered package would fail to boost dwindling confidence in Thailand, brokers said.
"I don't think the government can do anything. The best they can do is get an IMF loan and follow IMF rules. That is the best they can do," said a broker at a Bangkok Bank affiliate.
Concerns surrounding the plan's details, implementation and political acceptability saw the market go into lunch slightly off earlier highs as short term speculators took profits, brokers said.
But the market was expected to remain bouyant in the afternoon session on the broader news, brokers said.
"I don't think anything can really scare investors here anymore, as we are in the worst crisis ever," the broker said.
Banking, finance and communications issues were all sharply higher. Bangkok Bank Plc added nine 180, Dhana Siam Plc gained 3.75 to 41.75 and TelecomAsia was up 3.50 to 44.50.
